device.description: 12-bit 4-channel high-voltage (up to 40 V / +-20 V) output DAC with 2.5-V reference and SPI interface
device.note: dac81404.pdf (SLASEH2A) p.3-4 pinout (Table 6-1), p.6 recommended operating conditions, p.13-15 timing (7.6-7.11), p.29-30 register structure, update, broadcast, clear, reset, p.31-33 access cycle, daisy chain, CRC (Tables 8-2 to 8-6), p.34-40 register map

registers.name: DEVICEID
registers.note: p.35 Table 8-9: register reset 0920h for DAC61404, VERSIONID 0 (subject to change)

registers.name: BRDCAST
registers.note: p.39 Table 8-18: write-only; MSB aligned {DATA[11:0], x, x, x, x} (the 4 don't-care bits are stored as written)

registers.name: DACA
registers.note: p.40 Table 8-19: DAC buffer register (write-only), MSB aligned; reset 0000h

registers.name: DACA_ACT
registers.note: internal: the DAC-A active register (drives OUTA)

registers.name: DACB_ACT
registers.note: internal: the DAC-B active register (drives OUTB)

registers.name: DACC_ACT
registers.note: internal: the DAC-C active register (drives OUTC)

registers.name: DACD_ACT
registers.note: internal: the DAC-D active register (drives OUTD)

commands.name: BRDCAST
commands.note: p.29: BRDCAST loads the buffer registers of the channels with DACn-BRDCAST-EN = 1; their outputs then update per their sync mode (asynchronous: at once)

commands.name: Write DACA
commands.note: p.29: asynchronous mode updates the active register at SYNC rising

commands.name: Write DACB
commands.note: p.29: asynchronous mode updates the active register at SYNC rising

commands.name: Write DACC
commands.note: p.29: asynchronous mode updates the active register at SYNC rising

commands.name: Write DACD
commands.note: p.29: asynchronous mode updates the active register at SYNC rising

commands.name: Write
commands.note: p.31 Table 8-2: R/W = 0, bit 22 don't care, A[5:0], DI[15:0]; the next frame echoes it on SDO (daisy chain)

commands.name: Read
commands.note: p.31 Table 8-3: the next access cycle shifts out RW, bit 22, A[5:0] and the register

commands.name: BRDCAST (CRC frame)
commands.note: p.29: BRDCAST loads the buffer registers of the channels with DACn-BRDCAST-EN = 1; their outputs then update per their sync mode (asynchronous: at once)

commands.name: Write DACA (CRC frame)
commands.note: p.29: asynchronous mode updates the active register at SYNC rising

commands.name: Write DACB (CRC frame)
commands.note: p.29: asynchronous mode updates the active register at SYNC rising

commands.name: Write DACC (CRC frame)
commands.note: p.29: asynchronous mode updates the active register at SYNC rising

commands.name: Write DACD (CRC frame)
commands.note: p.29: asynchronous mode updates the active register at SYNC rising

commands.name: Write (CRC frame)
commands.note: p.33 Table 8-4: R/W = 0, CRC-ERROR, A[5:0], DI[15:0], CRC

commands.name: Read (CRC frame)
commands.note: p.33 Table 8-6: the next cycle shifts out R/W, CRC-ERROR (0), A[5:0], the register and the CRC

protocol.note: p.31: fewer than 24 (32 with CRC-EN) SCLK falling edges: ignored; more: only the first 24 (32) bits are used; registers update at SYNC rising; p.30, p.39: SOFT-RESET = 1010 resets, SOFT-CLR clears, SOFT-LDAC loads the synchronous-mode DACs

pages: p.3-4 (pinout), p.6 (ROC), p.13-15 (timing), p.29-30 (register structure, broadcast, clear, POR), p.31-33 (serial interface, CRC), p.34-40 (registers)
notModeled: analog outputs, sense pins, output ranges (DACRANGE stored only), reference, power-down states and thermal alarm

clear code: zero for unipolar ranges, midscale for bipolar ranges, per channel; the model takes the code for every channel from DACA-RANGE, so a channel whose range differs from channel A's clears to channel A's code
FAULT open-drain pin (CRC, thermal and DAC-busy alarms) and the STATUS alarm bits: never asserted
CRC: with CRC-EN = 1 the 32-bit frames are decoded but the CRC byte is not checked, CRC-ALM is never set and the CRC byte shifted out is 0
SDO-EN = 0 (SDO not operational) and FSDO: SDO always drives while SYNC is low
write-only registers (NOP, DACRANGE, TRIGGER, BRDCAST, DACn per Table 8-7): the model returns the stored value on read-back
daisy chain beyond one 24-bit echo; the 1-ms POR delay, 2.4-us update and 4-us broadcast waits; DEV-PWDWN power-down
variants: 12-bit version of DAC81404 (dac81404.pdf): same pinout, registers and protocol; DEVICEID 0920h, data MSB aligned {DATA[11:0], x, x, x, x} in the 16-bit DAC and BRDCAST words
